summary: Practise visual data preparation, PyTorch fine-tuning, evaluation, and OpenCV inference integration. Explore the 10-day course outline.
lede: Computer vision with OpenCV and PyTorch uses Python workflows to prepare visual data and evaluate image or video models. It is designed for intermediate Python practitioners, including computer vision, machine learning, and applied AI engineers, who work with visual predictions. Learn to inspect labels and create leakage-aware dataset splits, apply aligned preprocessing and augmentation, fine-tune classification or detection models, and review errors before building an OpenCV-to-PyTorch inference prototype.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate practitioners who use Python to process visual data, train or fine-tune models, and assess image or video predictions. It suits technical roles that connect dataset quality, model behaviour, and inference workflows.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Python and basic experience with image or video data is expected. Familiarity with machine-learning model training and evaluation will help you complete the practical work. Programming is required for course exercises. Advanced model and deployment topics receive operational application or conceptual coverage rather than production-engineering depth.
